question: Which letter code of Köppen climate characterises a hot-summer humid continental climate?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dfa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dfa** is the Köppen climate classification code for a hot-summer humid continental climate.
 
• Regions with a **Dfa climate** experience hot, humid summers and cold, snowy winters.
 
• These climates are typically found in the interior regions of continents, away from oceanic influences.
 
• Examples of areas with Dfa climates include parts of the Midwestern United States, southeastern Canada, and northern China.
 
• The classification is defined by average temperatures above **22°C** (72°F) in the warmest month and below **-3°C** (27°F) in the coldest month.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Köppen Climate Classification**

 
 
• A widely used climate classification system developed by climatologist Wladimir Köppen in 1884.
 
• It categorizes climates based on average monthly and annual temperature and precipitation.
 
• The system includes five main climate groups: Tropical (A), Dry (B), Temperate (C), Continental (D), and Polar (E).
 
• Subcategories further refine the classification based on seasonal patterns and temperature variations.
 
 
 
• **Continental Climates (Group D)**
 
 
• Characterized by significant seasonal temperature variations due to their location far from oceanic moderating effects.
 
• These climates are divided into subtypes like Dfa (hot-summer), Dfb (warm-summer), and Dfc (cold-summer).
 
• Typically found in the interiors of continents, such as North America, Europe, and Asia.
 
 
 
• **Hot-Summer Humid Continental Climate (Dfa)**
 
 
• Defined by hot summers with average temperatures above 22°C (72°F).
 
• Winters are cold, with temperatures frequently dropping below freezing.
 
• Precipitation is evenly distributed throughout the year, with occasional snow during winter months.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Dfa Regions**
 
 
• Midwestern United States (e.g., Chicago, Detroit).
 
• Southeastern Canada (e.g., Toronto, Ottawa).
 
• Northern China (e.g., Beijing).
 
• Parts of Eastern Europe (e.g., Kyiv).
